patch.summary:
Thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in ecommerce, but documented company-size audiences diverge.

Same category, different company size. Choose Magento only if your buying job matches “Open-source Magento core (free) plus Adobe Commerce enterprise licenses (GMV quote) — deep” rather than Webflow's shape. Choose Webflow only if your buying job matches “Design-led website platform with Ecommerce — Standard $29/mo (500 items, 2% fee), Plus $74” rather than Magento's shape. Workflow advantage: Magento leans catalog-management, wholesale-b2b; Webflow leans website-builder-commerce. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in ecommerce, but documented company-size audiences diverge.
- Positioning: Magento is Open-source Magento core (free) plus Adobe Commerce enterprise licenses (GMV quote) — deep catalog/B2B with high hosting and agency TCO.; Webflow is Design-led website platform with Ecommerce — Standard $29/mo (500 items, 2% fee), Plus $74 highlighted (5,000 items, 0% fee), Advanced $212 .
- Company-size focus: Magento (mid-market, enterprise) vs Webflow (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Magento-leaning catalog-management, wholesale-b2b, order-fulfillment vs Webflow-leaning website-builder-commerce.
- Researched limits: Magento — Operational and agency TCO is high versus hosted SaaS even when the Open Source license is $0; Webflow — Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the $29 floor alone.

Limitations — Magento: Operational and agency TCO is high versus hosted SaaS even when the Open Source license is $0; Adobe Commerce pricing is opaque (GMV quote) — hard to compare without a partner worksheet; Webflow: Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the $29 floor alone; Catalog caps (500 / 5,000 / 15,000 items) and Standard’s 2% transaction fee trail Shopify-class commerce OS depth.

Poor-fit cases: Magento is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Operational and agency TCO is high versus hosted SaaS even when the Open Source license is $0 · Webflow is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the $29 floor alone · Avoid Magento if you actually need Webflow's motion (Design-led website platform with Ecommerce — Standard $29/mo (500 items, 2% fee))

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
